# Step laws and endpoint traces

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> Two processes on the same configurations and moves take the same steps exactly when they have the same finite traces with both endpoints kept; traces of one move suffice. Feasible words alone lose the law.

Documentary review UTC: `2026-10-25T15:09:23+00:00`. Run the registry checker for source drift; this page is not a fresh proof receipt.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

A law is fixed by its traces: two processes on the same configurations and moves take the same steps exactly when they have the same finite traces with both endpoints kept, traces of one move sufficing. Forgetting endpoints loses the law: the process that stays put and the one that flips a bit take the same words from every configuration and end differently after one move, so they do not take the same steps.

Canonical source: [Labelled.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Labelled.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>

- Common State and Action types, supplied Process.step relations, and the existing Trace definition.

The actual interpretation of states, actions and steps remains supplied.
